page.name: Name

page.titlesDescription: The small model titles each conversation.

page.cloudsDescription: Each Cloud takes these at its next start. An empty field uses the server’s setting. A disk that’s already larger keeps its size.
page.idleDescription: A Cloud with no work for this long stops. An always-on Cloud never does.
page.sizeProblem: Enter a whole number, at least 1, or leave it empty.
page.deleteDescription: Its conversations, Clouds and shared folder are deleted. Its usage stays.
page.deleteBody: Its conversations, Clouds and shared folder are deleted, and its token stops working at once. You can’t undo this.

users.sessionsDescription: Ends every session of theirs, on every device.

sharing.label: Providers
sharing.description: When shared, every user uses the providers you set up.
sharing.descriptionApiKeys: When shared, every user uses the API keys you set up and their own subscriptions.

share.title: Share your providers with every user?
share.body: Every user’s model menu offers your providers instead of their own. Theirs stay saved and come back if you stop sharing.
share.subscriptions: Each user keeps their own subscriptions, which nobody else can use.

stop.title: Stop sharing your providers?
stop.body: Every user goes back to their own providers. Users who haven’t set any up have no models until they do.

confirm.add: Confirm it’s you to add an account.
confirm.resetPassword: Confirm it’s you to reset a password.
confirm.newPassword: Confirm it’s you to make a new password.

ready.added: The account for {email} is ready. Give them this password, or sign them in with the code below.
ready.reset: {email} has a new password. Give them this password, or sign them in with the code below.

reset.title: Reset {name}’s password?
reset.body: Demi makes a new first password and shows it once. Their current password stops working. Signed-in browsers and passkeys stay.

signOutEverywhere.title: Sign {name} out everywhere?
signOutEverywhere.body: Every browser signed in as {name} returns to the sign-in page. They can sign in again.

disable.title: Disable {name}’s account?
disable.body: {name} is signed out everywhere and can’t sign in. Their Cloud stops and their devices disconnect.
disable.note: Nothing is removed. Enable restores access.

cloud.title: Cloud
cloud.description: How the Clouds on this server are isolated and which networks they reach.

isolationDescriptions.simple: Each Cloud has its own system and files. This protects against mistakes, not against a program that tries to break out.
isolationDescriptions.gvisor: Each Cloud runs in a gVisor sandbox, which also stops a program that tries to break out.

download.hint: Downloads gVisor, about 160 MB, the first time
download.moving: Stopped Clouds move to gVisor once it’s downloaded, and running ones once they stop. Their files and installed packages move with them.

cloud.moving: Stopped Clouds move to {isolation} now, and running ones once they stop. Their files and installed packages move with them.
cloud.noNetworkPolicy: Clouds on Simple Isolation share the server’s network, so the network policy doesn’t apply.

policyDescriptions.noNetwork: Clouds reach nothing on any network.
policyDescriptions.developerServices: Clouds reach only the services builds download from, such as GitHub, npm and PyPI.
policyDescriptions.internetOnly: Clouds reach the internet, and nothing on the server’s private network.
policyDescriptions.internetAndPrivateNetwork: Clouds reach the internet and every private address, as a computer on the server’s network does, so a web page a Cloud’s browser opens can try to reach your internal services too.
policyDescriptions.custom: Clouds reach only what’s allowed below.

cloud.neverReachable: The server itself, cloud metadata services and other people’s Clouds are never reachable.
cloud.domainsAndAddressesDescription: Clouds reach each one listed: on every port, or only on the port written after it. While the internet is off, a name resolves only if it’s listed.
cloud.placeholder: Add domains or addresses, such as *.example.com or 10.20.0.7:22

problems.entry: Enter a domain, such as git.example.com or *.example.com, or an IPv4 address or network, such as 10.20.0.0/16.
problems.neverReachable: Clouds can never reach this address.

cloud.pending: Saved. Clouds get the change once the machine manager is available again.
